Link component, underlined by default.
TextField bundles label, input, helper text and error state in one component. Far less markup than composing primitives.

error + helperText cover the three client-side cases. server-rejected has no library channel: MUI has no form-level error API equivalent to React Aria's Form validationErrors, so it is component state we manage.
disabled on Button, TextField and Select.

Same, 40 options, with a maxHeight on the menu paper.
Same, 400 options. Renders all 400 MenuItems; MUI Select has no built-in virtualisation.
Autocomplete with multiple. Removable chips come free via renderValue and getItemProps. Notably stronger than React Aria, which has no multiselect component and needs ListBox + TagGroup composed.
Autocomplete filters as you type. filterOptions caps the rendered list at 100 for the 400-item fixture, which is a documented prop rather than a workaround.
DatePicker from the free @mui/x-date-pickers.

THE BLOCKER, resolved by composition per docs/requirements.md. MUI's range pickers exist only in @mui/x-date-pickers-pro, licence 'SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE' (commercial). Verified empirically: the community package ships ZERO Range* components. Composed from two free DateTimePickers with ampm=false and minute views, minDateTime/maxDateTime wired between them, and the span derived in application code. See EVIDENCE.md for exactly what this loses.
Dialog with DialogTitle/Content/Actions. Focus trap and Escape verified by e2e.
Tooltip, hover and keyboard-focus triggered by default.
Popover with anchorEl and outside-click dismiss.
Accordion + AccordionSummary + AccordionDetails, single-expand via controlled expanded state.

Card + CardContent exist, unlike React Aria. Matching the host is the work: MUI's Card has its own elevation, radius and padding opinions, so variant=outlined and elevation=0 are needed to reach Delta's flat bordered cards.
List + ListItemButton with selected state.
DataGrid over all 250 rows. Column type formatting via valueFormatter with Intl, driven by the active locale.
Built into DataGrid with an initial sortModel. No comparator written, in contrast to React Aria where sorting cost 22 lines.
checkboxSelection, with header select-all included.
showToolbar gives the built-in filter UI. No predicate written.
paginationModel plus pageSizeOptions. Entirely native, where React Aria has no pagination component at all and needed 34 custom lines. The single clearest advantage MUI has in this evaluation.

resizable: true per column. Verified that GridColDef.resizable and disableColumnResize exist in the community build, while disableColumnReorder appears in its Pro-omit list, so reorder is Pro-only. The brief accepts either.
DataGrid loading prop with a linear-progress overlay, localeText.noRowsLabel for empty, and Alert for error/success with correct ARIA roles.
LinearProgress and Alert. No custom banner markup, unlike React Aria which needed role=alert/status by hand.
ToggleButtonGroup, exclusive.

THREE steps, not the two this evaluation first did. (1) dir, (2) direction on the theme itself so the theme is rebuilt per locale with createTheme(base, { direction }), and (3) an emotion CacheProvider carrying @mui/stylis-plugin-rtl, which is the step that flips the CSS MUI emits. adapterLocale must also be threaded into LocalizationProvider. React Aria needed only I18nProvider and zero custom lines. Steps 1 and 2 alone LOOK right - components that read theme.direction in JS flip - while every physical offset stays put, which is how this run previously recorded a blocker that was its own omission. 23 lines for the provider plus 6 for the theme rebuild, and 2 dependencies.

Clean at all three viewports: 0px horizontal overflow in German at 390, 1024 and 1440. Notably better than the React Aria run, which overflowed 261px at 390px. Two small CSS rules help the DataGrid header wrap.
Host and candidate button, table, card and nav list rendered adjacent in section 9.

theming.method: createTheme() mapping the TypeScript token export into MUI's theme object: palette, typography, spacing, shape, zIndex, plus two components overrides for the focus ring. MUI theming is JavaScript, not CSS custom properties, so the theme is a build-time COPY of token values rather than a live reference: changing a token needs a rebuild, where a var()-based consumer would pick it up at runtime.
escapeHatchesUsed: cssVariables: true deliberately NOT enabled. It makes MUI emit its own --mui-* custom properties at :root level, placing MUI's palette in the same global scope as the host and defeating containment.
Two CSS rules reach into library-generated class names (.MuiDataGrid-root, .MuiDataGrid-columnHeaderTitle) to cap grid width and wrap long header labels. Recorded as overridesLibraryInternals: true.

MUI's picker prop types are not compatible with exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true. minDateTime/maxDateTime are typed as Date rather than Date | undefined, so a conditional spread is needed instead of `value ?? undefined`.
Stack no longer accepts flexWrap/alignItems as direct props in v9; they must move into sx.

None needed for portalled overlays, which is a genuine advantage here. MUI portals its popper to document.body, outside the .undrr-tokens element, and a computed-style check confirms it sees an EMPTY --undrr-color-surface there -- yet it still renders rgb(255,255,255) correctly, because the theme resolved token values at build time and emotion emitted literal colours. The react-aria run had to apply the token scope class to every overlay to avoid transparent popovers. The same build-time inlining that prevents runtime theming is what makes MUI immune here.

humanReviewRequired: MUI RTL is clean after its documented three-step setup: dir, a direction-aware theme and @mui/stylis-plugin-rtl. The route adds 29 integration lines, two dependencies and a provider; omitting the third step fails silently, so the setup belongs in any shared delivery standard.

axe `color-contrast` (1 serious): the helper text on the disabled TextField fails contrast. MUI applies its disabled text colour to the associated helper text, and the neutral token palette's --undrr-color-text-disabled (#8b9aa5) is roughly 2.8:1 on white. Disabled *controls* are exempt from WCAG 1.4.3, but helper text is not itself a disabled control, so this needs a ruling. Tokens are import-only so it could not be fixed here.

axe reported 4 incomplete rules it could not decide: aria-prohibited-attr, aria-valid-attr-value, color-contrast, duplicate-id-aria. `duplicate-id-aria` on a DataGrid page is worth a human look, since duplicate ARIA ids break screen-reader association.

The 400-option Select renders all 400 MenuItems. MUI Select has no built-in virtualisation; Autocomplete was capped at 100 rendered options instead. Whether the plain Select is acceptable at that size is a performance decision not taken here.

Keyboard and screen-reader testing by a human, particularly the composed date-time range: two separate pickers give screen-reader users two unrelated fields with no single accessible name for the range as a concept.

Omitting CssBaseline is a real deviation from MUI's intended setup. ScopedCssBaseline was used instead, which contains the reset but means MUI components run without the global normalisation they are built to expect. Needs a decision on whether that trade is acceptable, or whether the host should absorb CssBaseline.

The composed range's minDateTime/maxDateTime wiring is present in code but was NOT verified end to end: the calendar opens on a month with no out-of-range days, so no disabled day exists to assert against. Verified by reading the props only.
